newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Mir commander to have medical check - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russian Mir commander to have medical check - Tass.

text.p: The Russian commander of the crew on the space station Mir will undergo medical tests on Sunday to check on a heart problem, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Vasily Tsibliyev suffered an irregular heartbeat after a failed docking manoeuvre on June 25 in which the Spektr module attached to Mir was holed and the space station's power supply was damaged.
Tass quoted an official at Korolyov Mission Control outside Moscow as saying Tsibliyev's condition was gradually "normalising" but added: "He will have another medical examination today."
Tass described the situation on Mir as "normal" after a rest day on Saturday.

The crew, which also comprises Russian flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin and British-born NASA physicist Michael Foale, fixed their latest problem on Friday by restoring Mir's orientation -- lost when a computer crashed due to human error.
Space officials have delayed risky repairs to fix the power supply and have made clear they are likely to leave the repairs to a crew which is due to arrive on Mir on August 7.
Vladimir Solovyov, the Russian mission director, said on Saturday a final announcement on the repair plans was expected to be made on Monday.
